help.title: Help — Routes
help.recordStep1: Tap REC to start recording your outing.
help.recordStep2: Pause suspends recording; STOP ends it and lets you name the track.
help.recordStep3: On Android, recording keeps running in the background with the screen off.
help.prepareStep1: Tap “Create a route”, then place your points on the map (long press).
help.prepareStep2: Choose the profile and pace, then start the calculation.
help.prepareStep3: Save the draft to find it in Library, or go straight to guidance.
help.importStep1: File: tap “Import GPX” and choose a .gpx file.
help.importStep2: Received file: open it with SunTrail (“Open with”) or share it from another app.
help.importStep3: Tip: when Android asks which app to use, pick SunTrail then “Always”.
help.importStep4: Garmin, Komoot, Wikiloc: export the GPX from their website, then open it with SunTrail.
help.guidanceStep1: Open a route then tap “Follow this route” to start guidance.
help.guidanceStep2: Follow the next cue and remaining distance; guidance keeps running in the background (Android).
help.guidanceStep3: Tap STOP to end guidance; the track stays in Library.

label.tooltipExaggeration: Relief exaggeration: visually amplifies elevation to better read the terrain. 1x = realistic, 1.5x = pronounced, 3x = very exaggerated.
label.tooltipFogDistance: Fog distance: visual range of the 3D fog. Reducing this value improves performance on less powerful devices.
label.tooltipResolution: Resolution (LOD): terrain mesh detail level. 16 = very low (fast), 256 = ultra fine (performance-heavy).
label.tooltipRange: Render radius: number of terrain tiles loaded around the camera. Larger radius = wider view but higher memory usage.
label.tooltipVegDensity: Vegetation density: number of 3D trees rendered in forest areas. 0 = no trees, 15000 = dense forest.
label.tooltipWeatherDensity: Weather intensity: number of rain/snow particles visible in 3D. Affects graphics performance.
label.tooltipWeatherSpeed: Weather speed: movement speed of rain/snow particles. 1.0 = normal.
label.tooltipWeatherOpacity: Weather opacity: visual transparency of rain particles. 0.1 = nearly invisible, 1.0 = opaque.

disclosure.title: Access to your location
disclosure.body:
SunTrail uses your GPS position to center the map on your location and record your hiking routes.

Your coordinates stay on your device and are never sent to SunTrail servers. They may be transmitted to mapping services (MapTiler, OpenStreetMap) solely to load the tiles corresponding to your position.

mountain.title: Mountain Alert
mountain.comfortTooltip: Calculated from temperature, humidity, wind, precipitation, UV, visibility and weather code.
mountain.comfortScale: Score out of 10 — higher is better
mountain.tooltipFreezingLevel: Freezing level: altitude above which temperatures drop below 0°C. Risk of snow and ice if your route exceeds this altitude.
mountain.tooltipDewPoint: Dew point: temperature at which humidity condenses. The closer the dew point is to the temperature, the more humid and uncomfortable the air.
mountain.tooltipVisibility: Visibility: distance at which objects can be distinguished. <1 km = dense fog, <5 km = mist, >10 km = good visibility.
mountain.tooltipUV: UV Index: 0-11+ scale measuring solar radiation intensity. 0-2 = low, 3-5 = moderate, 6-7 = high, 8-10 = very high, 11+ = extreme. Sun protection recommended from index 3.

status.noTerrainHint: Sun times and position are still calculated. Terrain shade, first light and sunlight duration require elevation data.

stat.tooltipAzimuth: Azimuth: sun direction relative to north (0°=N, 90°=E, 180°=S, 270°=W). Helps anticipate which slopes will be sunlit.
stat.tooltipElevation: Elevation: sun height above horizon (0°=horizon, 90°=zenith). Elevation determines light intensity and ground-level heat.

acceptance.title: Important information before use

item1.title: Planning aid tool only
item1.desc: SunTrail is not a rescue device. In case of emergency, contact 112.

item2.title: Approximate GPS and 3D data
item2.desc: GPS signals can be inaccurate in mountains. 3D terrain is based on digital models with 5–25m resolution.

item3.title: Indicative solar simulation
item3.desc: Calculations do not account for weather, clouds, or unmodeled local obstacles.

item4.title: Slopes and avalanche risk
item4.desc: Slope shading (>30°) does not replace terrain analysis and the 3×3 risk reduction method.

item5.title: Carry an external battery
item5.desc: Heavy GPS and 3D rendering use quickly drains the battery. Always carry a paper map.

acceptance.legal: By continuing, you accept SunTrail's terms of use and acknowledge having read this safety information.
